question: Which oncogenes are able to induce cellular senescence?

Cdk2 suppresses cellular senescence induced by the c-myc oncogene
Here we report that the suppression of the c-Myc (MYC) oncogene induces cellular senescence in diverse tumor types including lymphoma, osteosarcoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma.

MYC overexpression is thought to initiate tumorigenesis by inducing cellular proliferation and growth and to be restrained from causing tumorigenesis by inducing cell cycle arrest, cellular senescence, and/or apoptosis.
We have found that expression of such an oncogene, Akt, causes senescence in primary mouse hepatoblasts in vitro.
Activated RAS/BRAF oncogenes induce cellular senescence as a tumor-suppressive barrier in early cancer development, at least in part, via an oncogene-evoked DNA damage response (DDR).

initial_executor.limitations: Evidence distinguishes between oncogene activation (Ras, Raf, Akt, Myc) inducing senescence and oncogene suppression (c-Myc) inducing senescence. Some evidence specifies cell types (fibroblasts, hepatoblasts) or conditions (p53 status). c-Abl is described as regulating senescence via tumor suppressors, not directly inducing it as an oncogene in the provided text.

We review and discuss here evidence for Myc-induced senescence - which is detectable to a limited degree as a cell-autonomous, direct response to Myc action, but occurs predominantly in a non-cell-autonomous fashion via crosstalk of the oncogene-driven cell population with non-neoplastic bystanders, namely cells of the host immune system, prompting them to release pro-senescent cytokines that strike back onto adjacent proliferating tumor cells.
